Windows, bounds and anchors

Source: R/lang_v2.R
omop_window.Rd

omop_window(start, end, anchor) is an inclusive range of whole days relative to an anchor (default the index date). NULL (or -Inf for start, Inf for end) leaves an endpoint unbounded. Each endpoint may instead be an omop_bound(anchor, offset) with its own anchor, so start and end can be anchored independently (e.g. on-treatment follow-up ending 30 days after the treatment course).

Usage

omop_window(start = NULL, end = NULL, anchor = "index")

omop_bound(anchor, offset = 0L)

omop_anchor(
  event,
  which = c("first", "last", "nth", "latest_end"),
  n = 1L,
  field = c("start", "end"),
  scope = c("person", "episode"),
  search = NULL
)

Arguments

start, end

Day offsets, NULL/-Inf/Inf, or omop_bound().

anchor

Anchor of integer offsets (default "index").

offset

Integer day offset of a bound.

event

An omop_event, omop_era or registry name.

which

"first", "last", "nth" or "latest_end".

n

Row number for which = "nth".

field

"start" or "end" of the selected row.

scope

"person" (default, may precede the index) or "episode".

search

NULL or an omop_window() restricting candidates.

Value

omop_window, omop_bound or omop_anchor objects.

Details

Anchors are "index", "index_end", "observation_start", "observation_end", an ISO date, or omop_anchor(event, ...): one complete event row selected by the order (start_date, source, key); field = "end" reads that row's end; latest_end selects by end (only with field = "end"); scope = "episode" confines the search to the episode's observed span; search is a window restricting the candidate rows. A missing anchor makes a window undefined (criteria UNKNOWN, reducers NA).

Examples

omop_window(-365, -1)
omop_window(omop_bound("index", 1), omop_bound("index_end", 30))
